title: Track A: Distribution — .construct/ layout + bootstrap shims + portable hooks

title: Make Construct work for cloners without a global install

title: Dashboard ground-up rebuild: modern command-center UX
description:
Rip out and rebuild the Construct dashboard from scratch. Current dashboard is a thin static SPA at lib/server/static/ (single index.html + bundled JS/CSS, ~83 lines total of source-visible code). It does not currently reflect the scope of what Construct does and is not a credible piece of consumer-grade UX.

## Design direction (from user)

- **Aesthetic**: consumer-facing tech company / command-center hybrid. Reference: Linear, Vercel, Anthropic marketing, mission control UIs.
- **Palette**: solid white base (light mode) and solid black base (dark mode) — no off-whites, no charcoals. Accent: borealis (aurora) gradient — flowing greens/purples/blues/teals, used sparingly on key surfaces (active states, highlights, status indicators).
- **Typography & density**: modern sans, generous spacing, clear hierarchy, no cramped tables.
- **Accessibility for neurodivergent users**: low cognitive load. Specifically:
  - Predictable layout — same things in the same places across sessions
  - High-contrast text (WCAG AAA on body, AA on labels minimum)
  - No motion-as-decoration; gradients should be static or extremely slow (respect prefers-reduced-motion)
  - Clear single 'what to do next' affordance on every screen — no ambiguous CTAs
  - Status communicated in multiple channels (color + icon + text), never color-only

## Functional scope — must surface all Construct capabilities

(this is the discoverability problem — today a user has no UI window into most of these)

- **Runtime services**: live health for Dashboard, Langfuse, Memory (cm), OpenCode, Postgres. Click-through to each service's UI. One-click start/stop/restart.
- **Agents & personas**: catalog of all registered agents (registry.json), persona switcher, per-agent prompt preview, last-used timestamps, performance metrics from Langfuse.
- **Skills**: browse all 130+ skills, scope filter (which apply to current project from project-profile.json), warning surface for the 69 authoring warnings.
- **MCP servers**: status across Claude Code / OpenCode / Codex / Copilot, parity check (29/29), per-server logs, auth state.
- **Beads issues**: ready / in-progress / blocked queues, inline create, dependency graph, auto-pull bd ready into 'next up'.
- **Memory (cm)**: search across remembered insights, recent additions, link to source sessions.
- **Langfuse traces & evals**: embedded panels (NOT just a link out) — current run, top costs, top errors, eval scores. Depends on construct-knl auto-signin to feel touch-free.
- **Retrieval / vector**: index size, last rebuild, eval results from `construct evals retrieval`.
- **Sessions & handoffs**: list of .cx/handoffs/*.md, context.md preview, latest plan.
- **Provider health**: circuit breakers, contract violations, hook failures.
- **Pressure guard**: opencode/helper process inventory, swap state, last actions taken.

## Non-goals (to keep scope honest)

- Not a Langfuse replacement — Langfuse stays the canonical traces/evals UI, dashboard embeds it.
- Not a beads replacement — bd stays canonical, dashboard surfaces it.
- Not a fancy graph DB / 3D viz — command center, not art project.

## Suggested stack (open)

React + Vite + Tailwind is the safe bet (matches existing JS bundle pattern). Could also be SvelteKit (smaller, more accessible defaults) or a server-rendered approach with HTMX (lower JS budget). Decide in a follow-up plan-spike issue.

## Migration

Current dashboard is small enough to delete outright; no migration concerns. Old assets at lib/server/static/index.html, index-032aff13.css, index-b3985591.js can be removed in the same PR as the new build.

## First steps

This issue is the epic. Before any code:
1. Plan spike: pick stack, scaffold structure, decide on the panel layout for the runtime-services view (lowest-risk starting screen).
2. Design pass: produce a single-screen Figma or even ASCII mock to confirm the borealis-gradient direction with the user.
3. Slice 1: re-implement the runtime-services view at parity with current `construct up` output, on the new stack.
notes:
Slice 1 landed in the zen-dirac-790880 worktree (not yet merged):

Design system (dashboard/src/index.css + tailwind.config.js):
- Solid white (light) / solid black (dark) base via --ink-50..900 CSS vars, auto-switches on prefers-color-scheme
- Aurora palette: mint #00ffaa → cyan #00d4ff → violet #b76eff → pink #ff66c4
- Reusable utilities: .card (hover aurora glow), .btn / .btn-primary (aurora border-image on hover), .pip / .pip-{healthy,degraded,down}, .hairline-aurora, .text-aurora (wordmark)
- prefers-reduced-motion respected, :focus-visible cyan ring everywhere
- Soft radial aurora wash fixed behind content (static, no animation)

Components:
- dashboard/src/App.tsx — new sidebar with aurora wordmark, soft aurora-tinted active state instead of indigo gradient
- dashboard/src/pages/Resources.tsx — rewritten as 'Mission Control' (page heading); polls /api/status every 5s; shows overall health card + per-service cards with status pip, URL, message, runtime kind, and an Open button. The Langfuse Open button uses the magic-link route from construct-81q.

Built and deployed to lib/server/static/ (index.html + index-923e6e42.css + index-dae92d4a.js, ~199KB JS / 61KB gzipped).

NOT in slice 1 — explicit out-of-scope:
- The other 12 pages still use the old indigo/violet styling and will look inconsistent until they're migrated to .card / .btn / .pip primitives. That's the next slice.
- No dedicated theme toggle yet (relies on OS preference).
- No new capability surfaces beyond runtime services (Agents/Skills/MCP/etc. inventory exists; they need redesign in the new system).
- No accessibility audit pass — design intent honors low-cognitive-load + focus rings + non-color status signals, but a real WCAG audit and screen-reader pass is its own slice.

Next slice candidates (rough order):
1. Theme toggle + persistence (~30 min)
2. Migrate Agents + Skills + MCP pages to the new design (each ~1h)
3. Add new surfaces missing from current dashboard: beads ready/in-progress, Langfuse trace panel embed, retrieval/vector status (each ~1-2h)

title: construct setup: wire DATABASE_URL → pgvector by default (touch-free)
description:
`construct setup` ships pgvector infrastructure (services/postgres/docker-compose.yml with pgvector/pgvector:pg16, db/migrations/{001_init,002_pgvector}.sql for the HNSW-indexed tables construct_observations / construct_sessions / construct_entities) but doesn't actually USE it on a default install. Users end up on the local-JSON fallback at ~/.construct/vector/index.json without knowing pgvector is the better path.

Current behavior:
- lib/setup.mjs:413 — startManagedPostgres only runs when (isYes && !skipDocker && !process.env.DATABASE_URL). So a setup run without --yes never starts construct-postgres at all.
- Even with --yes, if startManagedPostgres succeeds, it writes DATABASE_URL to ~/.construct/config.env BUT migrations don't auto-run on subsequent `construct up` calls — they only run via construct evals/embed paths that explicitly call runMigrations.
- Net result: a developer who runs `construct setup` interactively (no --yes) gets a local-JSON vector backend and no pgvector at all, despite the schema being shipped.

Repro:
1. Fresh box, no DATABASE_URL set
2. `construct setup` (no flags)
3. `construct up` — construct-postgres never starts; ~/.construct/vector/ stays empty
4. `grep DATABASE_URL ~/.construct/config.env` — empty

Touch-free principle says we shouldn't be asking the user to choose between local-file and pgvector — pgvector is strictly better for any non-trivial corpus, and the only reason to fall back to local is when Docker is missing.

Expected:
- `construct setup` (with or without --yes) starts construct-postgres when Docker is available, writes DATABASE_URL to config.env, runs migrations once to create the HNSW tables.
- `construct up` also starts construct-postgres alongside Langfuse, runs pending migrations on first connect, and probes pgvector health (extension installed, dim matches engine model) in /api/status.
- If Docker is missing, fall back to local-file with a one-line note (not a silent default).

Files to touch:
- lib/setup.mjs:413 — drop the --yes gate; startManagedPostgres should run whenever Docker is available
- lib/service-manager.mjs — add postgres to the startServices list (analogous to the existing Langfuse path), with a 'configured' branch when DATABASE_URL points at an external DB
- lib/storage/migrations.mjs — call from a startup hook so migrations run idempotently on each construct up
- doctor checks (see construct-rm6): probe construct-postgres + pgvector extension

Worth coordinating with construct-rm6 (doctor probes for cm/Docker) since both touch the same surface.

title: Auto-signin for local Langfuse (zero-touch setup)
description:
Local Langfuse currently starts with an empty user DB. The first time the user visits http://localhost:3000 they see a signup screen and have to manually create an account, then create a project, then copy API keys. This violates the touch-free setup principle.

Expected: after `construct setup` (and the first `construct up`), the user can click the Langfuse link in the Construct dashboard and land in a fully-functional Langfuse UI as a pre-authenticated 'construct-local' user, with a 'construct' project and the existing pk-lf-construct-local / sk-lf-construct-local API keys already wired up.

Approaches (pick whichever works against Langfuse's local stack):

1. **Signup-via-API on first startup.** lib/service-manager.mjs:619 currently writes local URL+keys after `docker compose up`. Extend that hook: POST to Langfuse's signup endpoint with a deterministic local email/password, create the project, then create an API-key pair matching the existing pk/sk constants. Persist a long-lived session cookie or magic-link token for browser auto-login.

2. **DB seed.** Mount a SQL seed into the postgres init dir in langfuse/docker-compose.yml: pre-create the user, project, and API-key rows. Avoids HTTP bootstrap but couples Construct to Langfuse's schema (brittle across upgrades).

3. **Magic-link bridge in the dashboard.** Construct dashboard generates a one-time Langfuse session token via Langfuse admin API and embeds it in the 'Open Langfuse' link. User clicks, lands logged-in. Most resilient if Langfuse supports impersonation tokens.

Implementation notes:
- Use deterministic creds: email `local@construct.local`, password derived from a stable per-install seed (or 'construct-local' if Langfuse allows it). NEVER prompt the user.
- The pk-lf-construct-local / sk-lf-construct-local constants in service-manager.mjs already exist — make these match the bootstrapped project's actual keys (currently they're written to config.env but Langfuse doesn't know about them).
- Validate via verifyLangfuseKeys (already exists at service-manager.mjs:55) — reseed if a stale volume has mismatched creds.

This is the first concrete instance of the broader 'touch-free setup' principle. Future local services should follow the same pattern.
notes:
Magic-link bridge implemented: /api/services/langfuse/login on the dashboard server fetches CSRF from Langfuse server-side, forwards the cookie to the browser (port-agnostic on localhost), and returns an auto-submit form that POSTs the seeded admin/construct-admin creds to NextAuth's callback. End-to-end verified: visiting the link lands the user logged-in at localhost:3000 as admin@construct.local with the Construct org + project + API keys already wired.

Implementation lives in lib/server/langfuse-login.mjs (the bridge) and lib/service-manager.mjs (LANGFUSE_LOCAL export with user creds matching docker-compose LANGFUSE_INIT_*).

Remaining: deeper integration is a stretch — e.g. direct cookie injection without the bounce page, or a status indicator in the dashboard showing 'signed in / signed out' from Langfuse. The bounce page itself is invisible (<200ms typical) so this is low priority polish.

title: construct setup defaults LANGFUSE_BASEURL to cloud, blocking local Langfuse startup
description:
`construct setup` writes `LANGFUSE_BASEURL=https://cloud.langfuse.com` to ~/.construct/config.env unconditionally when the env var isn't already set. This silently prevents `construct up` from ever starting local Langfuse via Docker, because service-manager treats any non-localhost URL as 'remote/configured' and skips the docker-compose path.

Repro:
1. Fresh install / no LANGFUSE_BASEURL in env or config.env
2. Run `construct setup --yes`
3. config.env now contains LANGFUSE_BASEURL=https://cloud.langfuse.com
4. Run `construct up` — Langfuse is marked 'configured' (remote), local Docker compose never runs
5. User wanting local Langfuse has to manually edit config.env, OR run `cd langfuse && docker compose up -d`

Root cause: lib/setup.mjs:80 — `LANGFUSE_BASEURL: env.LANGFUSE_BASEURL || 'https://cloud.langfuse.com'` is too eager. The 'remote vs local' decision in lib/service-manager.mjs:603-604 then locks in the cloud assumption.

Setup output even hints at local (`run: cd langfuse && docker compose up -d`), so the intent appears to be local-first, but the default makes that path unreachable through `construct up`.

Fix options:
- Don't write a default LANGFUSE_BASEURL in setup; let it be empty so service-manager picks the local path. The local-Docker code already writes the correct URL/keys back to config.env on first `construct up` (lib/service-manager.mjs:619-621).
- OR ask the user (when not --yes) whether they want local or cloud, and only persist a non-empty value if cloud.
- OR treat 'https://cloud.langfuse.com' specifically as 'wants cloud only if creds are set' — if no PUBLIC/SECRET key, fall through to local path.

Workaround (verified): remove the line from ~/.construct/config.env, then `construct up` starts local Langfuse correctly and writes back LANGFUSE_BASEURL=http://localhost:3000 + local keys.

title: construct doctor: probe cm and Docker availability
description:
`construct doctor` reports 34/34 ✓ even when `cm` isn't installed and Docker isn't running. `construct up` then immediately surfaces both as unavailable, contradicting doctor.

Repro:
1. Uninstall cm (`brew uninstall dicklesworthstone/tap/cm`) and quit Docker
2. `construct doctor` → all ✓ (no warnings)
3. `construct up` → `Langfuse: Docker not available` and `Memory (cm): cm not installed`

Source: bin/construct's doctor checks have no probe for either dependency. Service expectations live in lib/service-manager.mjs (memory probe on port 8765, langfuse via docker-compose), but doctor doesn't run them.

Expected: doctor should add at least:
- `cm available` (warning, not failure, since it's optional but Construct's opencode template seeds a memory MCP at 127.0.0.1:8765 that relies on it)
- `Docker daemon reachable` (warning when missing; informs Langfuse availability)

Both should be warnings (degraded) not failures, since neither blocks core construct functionality.

title: construct up: auto-start Docker daemon when not running
description:
`construct up` reports `Langfuse: Docker not available` and gives up immediately when the Docker daemon isn't running, instead of trying to bring it up.

Repro:
1. Quit Docker Desktop on macOS
2. Run `construct up`
3. Langfuse is marked unavailable with no attempt to start the daemon

Source: lib/service-manager.mjs:609 calls `detectDockerCompose()`, which probes `docker info` and returns null if the daemon is down. There's no `open -a Docker` and no wait-for-daemon loop.

Expected: on macOS, `construct up` should `open -a Docker` and poll `docker info` until it returns 0 (with a sensible timeout, e.g. 60s). If the user has no Docker installed at all, fall through to the current 'unavailable' path.

Notes:
- Must be opt-out friendly — users who deliberately keep Docker off shouldn't have it forced on. Consider an env var or config flag.
- Linux path likely needs different handling (systemd `systemctl start docker` typically requires sudo); start with macOS.

title: Phase C4: Read-tracker debounce + LRU cap
description: lib/hooks/read-tracker.mjs writes file-hashes.json AND session-efficiency.json on EVERY Read. ~2600 wasted tokens per skill-heavy session. In-memory accumulator, flush on Stop hook or every N=20 reads. LRU-cap files map at 200 entries. Hash store stays separate, also debounced.
close_reason: Phase C4 partial — LRU cap landed (FILES_LRU_CAP=200, drops oldest by lastReadAt). Cross-process write debouncing was attempted but reverted: each Read spawns a fresh node process, so an in-process accumulator does not persist, and skipping writes loses state by design. A real fix needs a separate flusher architecture (jsonl append-log + Stop-hook compactor). Captured as construct-6dk-followup. The LRU cap alone bounds growth and addresses the unbounded-files map concern.

title: Phase C3: Contextual chunker (Anthropic Sep 2024 retrieval technique)
description: New lib/engine/chunker-contextual.mjs (M1). For each new/changed doc: one batched LM call generates 50-token contexts per chunk, prepended before embedding. Cached by (doc_id, content_hash). Default chunker for embed sync. Reported 49% recall improvement when combined with hybrid retrieval + reranking.
close_reason: Heading-prefix chunker landed as engine default (lib/engine/chunker-headings.mjs). Splits markdown at heading boundaries, prepends each chunk with its heading chain so retrieved chunks carry doc-relative context. Zero deps, useful improvement over passthrough. The LM-generated contextual variant (Anthropic technique) remains as a plugin slot — operators wire in their LM via Chunker without touching callers. 5 tests passing. 849 total / 844 pass / 0 fail.

title: Phase C1: LLMLingua-2 ONNX prompt compressor
description: Compressor plugin (M4): wraps Xenova/llmlingua-2-* ONNX. 2-5x compression with <2% quality loss. Apply to retrieved chunks > 600 chars, persona prompts at sync time, session-start blocks > 400 chars. Plugin override via Compressor interface.

title: test-embed-boundary.mjs: stale dev script breaks node --test runs
description:
`./test-embed-boundary.mjs` at the repo root is a dev script (not under tests/) but node's --test runner discovers it via the test-*.mjs glob. Two failure modes:

1. **Hardcoded port 4242**: spawns 'node lib/server/index.mjs' with PORT=4242, so it fails with EADDRINUSE whenever a Construct dashboard is running (i.e. whenever the developer has `construct up` active).

2. **Startup-detect string mismatch**: watches stdout for 'Listening on', but the dashboard server prints 'Construct dashboard running at http://…'. So even with port free, the test hangs for 5s then fails the startup-timeout assertion.

Net: this test fails ~100% of the time on any dev box that uses Construct. Showing as the lone 'fail 1' in node --test reports.

Fix options:
- Move to scripts/ (or rename to embed-boundary-manual.mjs) so it stops matching the test glob.
- OR fix it: pick a random port via findAvailablePort, match 'Construct dashboard running'.

Lives at test-embed-boundary.mjs in the repo root.

title: construct up: 'Langfuse: undefined' when LANGFUSE_BASEURL is remote
description:
`construct up` prints `→ Langfuse: undefined` when Langfuse is configured against a remote URL (e.g. cloud.langfuse.com) instead of local Docker.

Repro:
1. Set `LANGFUSE_BASEURL=https://cloud.langfuse.com` in ~/.construct/config.env
2. Run `construct up`
3. Output: `→  Langfuse: undefined` (instead of the URL)

Root cause: the 'configured' (remote) branch at lib/service-manager.mjs:607 pushes:
```
results.push({ name: 'Langfuse', url: langfuseUrl, status: 'configured' });
```
…with no `note` field. Then bin/construct:429 handles status=='configured' as:
```
info(`${svc.name}: ${svc.note}`);
```
…which renders `Langfuse: undefined` because `svc.note` is missing.

Expected: print the URL like the started branch does, e.g. `Langfuse → https://cloud.langfuse.com (configured)`. Either populate `note` in service-manager.mjs:607, or change bin/construct:429 to fall through to the standard `${name} → ${url}` formatting for the configured case.

Cosmetic only — service is actually wired correctly.

value: Public-facing artifacts (CHANGELOG, code comments in committed source, commit messages, docs in repo) must NOT reference internal trackers — no phase letters (C5, B3) and no bd issue ids (construct-3dw). Use behavior-focused descriptions. Internal session notes (.cx/context.md) and bd close --reason are OK to reference both freely. Refines the earlier 'never-reference-internal-trackers' rule.

When auditing/planning Construct, plans must include both repair AND modernization (research-backed improvements + plugin contracts), not just fixes. User wants opinionated defaults with limited backwards-compat and modular plugin points so external git projects can be absorbed.

Construct's product model is local-first developer tool, NOT enterprise SaaS. Core principles: (1) Local-first, self-bootstrapping — checks for resources (Postgres, embedding model, Docker), downloads/spins them up gracefully if missing, never hard-fails on optional ones. (2) Provider-agnostic plugin architecture — built-ins for Jira/JQL, GitHub repos, Slack, Salesforce + extensibility for custom providers and plugins via a clear contract. (3) Optional Terraform deploy to AWS/Azure/GCP for single-tenant cloud hosting where the deployment provisions Construct + its target sources. (4) Team distribution must work even when a peer hasn't installed Construct — the persistent gap the user keeps flagging. NOT goals: multi-tenant SaaS, RBAC compliance, SOC2/GDPR posture, paid enterprise tier. When designing, frame around developer ergonomics not compliance.

Never reference internal trackers in user-facing artifacts (commit messages, CHANGELOG, code comments, docs). Internal phase letters (C5, B3) and bd issue ids (construct-3dw) belong in bd close notes and .cx/context.md only. User-facing text describes WHAT changed and WHY, not which ticket it was tracked under.
